Cuphead is visually breathtaking. The hand-drawn 1930s cartoon animation is one of the most impressive art styles I’ve ever seen in a video game, and the music is so good. But beauty alone doesn’t make a game enjoyable, and after my time with it, I can’t recommend it for everyone.

This game is brutally hard, every boss fight demands perfect precision, pattern memorization, and lightning-fast reflexes. If you’re a newer player the learning curve will feel less like a curve and more like a brick wall. Even my veteran gamer friend has spent hours stuck on a single boss. If you’re buying this for a younger player or someone just getting into gaming, I’d strongly caution against it. It’s punishing in a way that stops being fun pretty quickly.

I had high hopes for co-op through Steam’s Remote Play Together, but honestly it was nearly unplayable for me. The input lag was severe, and in a game where surviving depends entirely on split-second timing to dodge attacks, any lag at all makes things nearly impossible. 

Bottom Line
If you’re a gamer who lives for a hardcore challenge and you’re playing solo on your own machine, Cuphead might be exactly what you’re looking for. But if you’re newer to gaming, buying it for a younger player, or hoping to enjoy it with a friend over Remote Play Together, I’d say either go in with very low expectations or skip it altogether.

citations.review_text:
Holy sh#t! I think I've just found a goldmine. I've still not completed the game because the levels are genuinely hard. But every time I fail, I end up loving the game even more.

After every defeat i don't now why, but i don't feel bad, i just feel "This game is so awesome—I want to try again." I think that's because after each failure I see the patterns more clearly and understand what I did wrong, so for next time now i know what exactly I need to do to make progress.

I know the things i described here is fairly common in souls-like/ metroidvania games but the difference is that those games usually comes with a certain level of frustration also [spoiler](i.e frustration of loosing every item/points)[/spoiler] . Though, here I found that frustration to be almost completely absent.

TL;DR: Yes, it’s a difficult game, and you’ll restart a lot. but every defeat makes the pattern more clear, so the more you lose, the more you learn.

Playing this game never makes me want to throw my controller or tear my hair out. Yes, it’s difficult, and you’ll lose and restart a lot—but the more you lose, the more you learn. You start picking up on enemy attack patterns and learning how to properly dodge projectiles. What really hooked me, though, is the soundtrack. The jazzy, old-school music is super refreshing and insanely catchy.

9.5/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features hand-drawn 1930s rubberhose animation paired with an authentic jazz soundtrack.

citations.review_text: Cuphead is an absolute masterpiece of indie gaming that perfectly marries punishing, run-and-gun gameplay with a stunning 1930s cartoon aesthetic. Every single frame of the game is beautifully hand-drawn and animated, backed by a phenomenal, authentic jazz soundtrack that keeps your energy high through every grueling boss battle. While the difficulty is notoriously steep, the tight controls, imaginative enemy designs, and instant restarts ensure that every defeat feels like a learning experience rather than a frustration. It is a visually spectacular, highly rewarding triumph of game design that captures the golden age of animation while delivering some of the most satisfying combat in modern gaming.

So good and challenging! If you're a first time player it might seem to hard, but the game for what it is is amazing! With every frame of animation hand drawn in that rubberhose cartoon style and soundtrack that slaps, creative themes, hard but fair gameplay, it's PERFECT!!!

claims.claim: Players describe the game as extremely challenging and difficult, requiring pattern memorization and practice to overcome boss fights.

citations.review_text: This is one of my favorite games of all time. The Art and Music are great. If you're not used to the games of old this game is rather challenging. You need to learn the patterns and rhythms of all the levels. So much fun!

Cuphead is an excellent "Mega-Man-Like" action shooter, that is basically perfectly conceived and executed extremely well, with an amazing aesthetic that obviously took the developers a ton of effort to produce in the world before AI art generation. It's also gloriously difficult. A true "Gamer's Game," for those who want a hefty challenge in reaction time, enemy pattern recognition and memorization.

Aside from the art style, what's truly impressive about Cuphead is its subtle breakdown of gameplay variation, which is, I think, perfectly conceived. With Vanilla Cuphead (sans the DLC), there are 25 levels. 19 of those levels are boss battles, with 6 "run & gun" levels, that don't change the player's movement mechanics but change the objective of the level. Of the 19 bosses, 5 are designed with a more free flying SCHMUP plane mechanic which changes the player's movement mechanics while keeping the objective the same. And of the 12 remaining levels, 1 is a mini-boss gauntlet that creates a strategic endurance condition no other level attempts. The overall effect is that, while the core gameplay is always consistent enough to learn mastery, the key variations on the theme that occur mix up gameplay enough that you don't get bored, while allowing more specialized mastery of certain level types. This is basically peak game design on play-type variance, if nothing else. 

There are only a couple of flaws with Cuphead. The first is the opaqueness of the objective. This is usually just a boss health bar, but it isn't revealed until the player dies. This is done on purpose, and I believe I understand the thinking behind it (an enemy health bar is a distraction in the midst of battle, and removing the distraction means they can throw more attacks at the player fairly), but many players will not find this obfuscation preferable. One of the best games ever made. The gameplay is so fluid and satisfying to pull off, and it being hand animated adds so much charm and character. claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as very difficult and challenging, causing high levels of frustration or anger while still remaining fun.

citations.review_text:
I started playing Cuphead around three or four years ago, but I kept taking long breaks from it. A lot of my time with the game was spent playing on my PC with my best friend whenever he came over. We would sit there for hours, getting destroyed by the same boss again and again, then somehow convincing ourselves that the next attempt would definitely be the one.
After all those pauses, I finally came back and decided to finish everything properly, including the solo challenges. I ended up getting 300%, every achievement, every ability, and every possible S and P rank. The last part made me pretty angry at times, not going to lie, but finally completing it felt really satisfying.
There is quite a bit of RNG, and sometimes it can be annoying, but you eventually get used to it. Getting 300% can take around 18–25 hours for a skilled player, or maybe 40–60 for an average player.
Yeah, this game is difficult, frustrating, charming, and honestly a lot of fun. I recommend it to anyone who enjoys challenging games and does not mind failing a lot before finally winning.
I also enjoyed the cartoon, and I honestly cannot wait for the announced Mighty Cuphead Adventure and the next Cuphead sequel :D

If you still haven’t tried Cuphead, you really should give it a chance.
I definitely recommend it.
